Variants.Content: The Kargas family belonged to the local elite of Novos. Its status came from mansions, caravansaries, marriages, and adaptation to the city's religious order. Bearded monks can both bless betrothals and adjudicate taboos; if Kargos wants to last, wealth must appear as support for order rather than as an open challenge. Norvos is divided into the upper city on the cliff and the lower city by the river. Giant bells, stone steps and axe-bearing monks jointly maintain the theocratic order dominated by bearded monks. Caravans, carpets, armor, and inland roads brought wealth, but noble families still had to respect religious judgment.
Entry Kagos Wealth can buy guards and mansions, but it is difficult to openly disobey those who have masters of divine law and armed monks.
Entry Kagos The upper-city banquets were far away from them, but every religious decision fell down the stone steps to the market-place.

Entry Kagos Kargos is a local house in Norvos that maintains its position between theocracy, aristocratic life in the upper city, and commerce in the lower city. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
